title: Pigmented & epidermal birthmarks
summary: Naevus of Ota, achromic and anaemic naevi, Becker naevus, Mongolian spots and linear epidermal naevi. Mostly benign and needing reassurance, with key exceptions: the eye in Ota, tuberous sclerosis, and documenting Mongolian spots for safeguarding.

glance.think: A congenital or early-childhood patch: blue-grey (dermal melanocytosis), pale (achromic or anaemic), brown and hairy (Becker), or linear and warty (epidermal naevus).
glance.engine: Developmental pigment or mosaic abnormalities: dermal melanocytes, reduced melanin, vasoconstriction, or keratinocyte mosaicism.
glance.backbone: Reassure, offer camouflage, document carefully, and refer selectively for specialist laser or surgery.
glance.never_miss: Ocular Ota (glaucoma), multiple ash-leaf macules (tuberous sclerosis), extensive or syndromic epidermal naevus, and misreading a Mongolian spot as a bruise.

head: Birthmark
Colour / look
Typical site
Key point
rows: Forehead, temple, around the eye (V1/V2) ± sclera
Vasoconstriction, not melanin loss; NF1 association
Shoulder or upper trunk; men about 5:1
Rare Becker naevus syndrome (breast or pectoral hypoplasia)
**Document** to avoid confusion with bruising; most fade by about age 4
Trunk or limbs, usually one side

list: **Dermal melanocytoses** (Ota, Mongolian spot): melanocytes arrested in the dermis during embryonic migration (GNAQ/GNA11 mutations described).
**Achromic naevus:** a mosaic developmental pigment defect (melanocytes present, but melanin production or transfer reduced). It is not autoimmune.
**Naevus anaemicus:** localised α-adrenergic hypersensitivity of dermal vessels.
**Becker naevus:** a hamartoma of epidermis, melanocytes and hair follicles, triggered by androgens around puberty.
**Epidermal naevus:** postzygotic keratinocyte mosaicism (FGFR3, PIK3CA, HRAS).

features: See the table under ‘What it is’. Extra points:

list: Naevus of Ota: present at birth in about half; more common in East Asian women. Rarely, melanoma develops within dermal melanocytosis.
Naevus anaemicus: **diascopy** (pressing the surrounding skin) makes the contrast disappear.
Epidermal naevus: starts flat and tan, then becomes warty, and may extend through childhood. **ILVEN** is an itchy inflammatory variant.

diagnosis: Clinical, with Wood’s lamp and dermoscopy where helpful. Achromic naevus shows a faint residual network, unlike the ‘dead white’ of vitiligo. Biopsy is rarely needed.

head: Birthmark
Main differentials
rows: Mongolian spot, blue naevus, melasma, drug pigmentation, bruise
Vitiligo, ash-leaf macules (tuberous sclerosis), pityriasis alba, post-inflammatory hypopigmentation, naevus anaemicus, piebaldism
Café-au-lait macule, congenital melanocytic naevus, plexiform neurofibroma, smooth muscle hamartoma
**Bruising** (acute, tender, colour changes over time), naevus of Ota/Ito
Lichen striatus, linear lichen planus, linear porokeratosis, sebaceous naevus (scalp)

list: **Reassure.** Most need no medical treatment. Offer **camouflage** cosmetics.
**Naevus of Ota:** specialist laser (Q-switched Nd:YAG or picosecond) over several sessions. **Ophthalmology** if the eye is involved. Any changing nodule needs dermatology.
**Achromic naevus:** refer if there is doubt, especially with multiple ash-leaf-like macules (tuberous sclerosis work-up).
**Becker naevus:** sun protection reduces contrast. Hair removal (shaving, waxing, or specialist laser). Examine for breast or limb asymmetry if extensive.
**Mongolian spot:** no treatment. **Document site, size and colour** in the red book and notes.

**Epidermal naevus:** emollients. Specialist options include keratolytics, calcipotriol, laser or surgery (recurrence possible). Refer if extensive, syndromic, a scalp sebaceous naevus, or ILVEN. Do not treat as warts with destructive OTC products.

red_flags: Naevus of Ota involving the **sclera or eye**: glaucoma screening.
**Multiple** hypopigmented ash-leaf macules, seizures or developmental delay: tuberous sclerosis.
Extensive epidermal naevus with eye, neurological or skeletal features (epidermal naevus syndrome).
Extrasacral or atypical blue-grey marks without documentation: safeguarding questions. Document early.
pearls: Mottled blue-grey pigment around the eye is not ‘just a birthmark’ if the sclera is involved.
Clear documentation of Mongolian spots protects families from later misunderstanding.
Naevus anaemicus does not redden on rubbing, but vitiligo and achromic naevus do.
